title: Indexes — Overview
description: Learn what indexes are, why they matter, and the two main types of indexes in SQL Server.

data.text: Indexes are special data structures associated with tables or views that help speed up the retrieval of data. Think of an index like the index at the back of a book — instead of scanning every page, you can look up the topic and jump directly to the relevant pages.
A clustered index determines the physical order of data in a table. Each table can have only one clustered index because the data rows can only be sorted in one order.
A non-clustered index is a separate structure from the data rows. It contains a copy of the key columns and a pointer to the actual data rows. A table can have multiple non-clustered indexes.
How a Non-Clustered Index Resolves a Query

data.caption: A non-clustered index finds the key, then a key lookup fetches the remaining columns from the clustered index.
data.definition:
flowchart TD
  A[SELECT ... WHERE city = 'Berlin'] --> B{Index on city?}
  B -- yes --> C[Seek ix_customers_city]
  B -- no --> D[Scan the clustered index]
  C --> E{All columns covered?}
  E -- yes --> F[Return rows from the index]
  E -- no --> G[Key lookup into the clustered index]
  G --> F

data.title: Create and inspect an index on a temp table
data.content: This script creates a small table, adds a non-clustered index, and reads the index metadata back. Run it in any database.
data.code:
-- A heap: no clustered index yet
CREATE TABLE #Customers (
    customer_id INT NOT NULL,
    city        NVARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
    email       NVARCHAR(100) NOT NULL
);

CREATE INDEX ix_customers_city ON #Customers (city);

SELECT
    i.name        AS index_name,
    i.type_desc   AS index_type,
    c.name        AS column_name,
    ic.key_ordinal
FROM tempdb.sys.indexes  AS i
JOIN tempdb.sys.index_columns AS ic ON ic.object_id = i.object_id AND ic.index_id = i.index_id
JOIN tempdb.sys.columns  AS c ON c.object_id = ic.object_id AND c.column_id = ic.column_id
WHERE i.object_id = OBJECT_ID('tempdb..#Customers')
ORDER BY i.index_id, ic.key_ordinal;

data.title: Interview answer
data.text: Say that an index is a B-tree that lets SQL Server seek to the rows it needs instead of scanning the whole table, and that every index you add costs write performance and storage. A good answer names the three places indexes matter: WHERE predicates, JOIN keys, and ORDER BY.

data.title: Indexes Overview Key Points
points: Indexes speed up data retrieval at the cost of additional storage and maintenance overhead.
A clustered index physically orders the data rows; a non-clustered index stores a separate copy of key columns with pointers.
Each table can have only one clustered index but multiple non-clustered indexes.
Use indexes on columns frequently used in WHERE clauses, JOIN conditions, and ORDER BY clauses.
